frequency_question: How often does an executive agency successfully execute a formal revocation of a major institutional accreditor's status when the political principals explicitly demand it?
membership_rule: Federal actions where the Department of Education or equivalent cabinet-level oversight body formally terminates or strips an established national accrediting agency of its federal recognition.

cases.name: ED revocation of American Bar Association's law school accrediting recognition threat (historical review instances)
ED stripping of ACICS (Accrediting Council for Independent Colleges and Schools) recognition
ED second termination of ACICS recognition

provenance_note: 3 cases named, 5 claimed via skeleton x multiplier (1.7x)
coverage_note: 3 named; estimated 5 total major challenges in the window.
known_gaps: Does not capture informal backing-down where agencies capitulate to executive demands without a formal revocation order.
skeleton: Instances of major accrediting agency recognition reviews vs actual terminations over the past 30 years.
multiplier: 2 hits out of roughly 5 major high-stakes contestations involving national accrediting bodies where political principals exerted intense pressure.
validity_reason: Administrative law standards and the structural relationship between the Department of Education and recognized accreditors remain stable across this timeframe.
